The learned Assistant Judge, on justice. consideration of the evidence as adduced by the plaintiff and defendant No.1, decreed the suit on contest Against the aforesaid decree defendant No.1 as plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.1 of 1993 on 6-1-93 before the learned District Judge; Munshiganj with a nominal court-fee of Taka 5.00 only out of Taka 1910.00 with a prayer for time to file deficit court-fee subsequently and the learned District Judge allowed him time to file the deficit court-fee by 21-1-93. The defendant appellant did not file the deficit court-fee by 21-1-1993 the date fixed by the court for filing of the deficit court-fee but instead of filing the deficit court-fee he prayed for time to file the same. Thereafter the learned District Judge allowed time to the appellant opposite party No.1 to file the deficit court-fee by 4-2-1993. The defendant appellant failed to put in the deficit court fee on that date and also on subsequent dates and on the prayer of the defendant-appellant praying for time for filing the deficit court-fee the learned District Judge allowed the appellant opposite party time for putting in the deficit court-fee of Taka 1910.00 ti118-9-93, when opposite party No.1 filed the deficit court-fee. The learned District Judge thereafter fixed 15-9-93 for admission of the appeal and the appeal was admitted on that date although the appeal had already become barred by law. It is against this order the plaintiff- petitioner moved this court and obtained the Rule. 	. 

 6.	 Heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the revisional application, including the impugned order and also order Nos. 1-12 of the Title Appeal No. 1 of 1993 of the court of the District Judge, Munshiganj. It appears that defendant No.1 being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 22-11-1992 of Title Suit NO.7 of•1990 of the court of learned Assistant Judge Munshiganj preferred Title Appeal No.1 of 1993 before the court of learned District Judge on 6-1-1993 with a nominal court fee of Taka 5.00 only out of the required court fee of Taka 1910.00 with a prayer for time to file the deficit court-fee and the learned District Judge allowed time to file deficit court-fee by 21-1-1993. It further appears that defendant No.1 could not file the deficit court-fee on 21-1-1993 and prayed for further time to file the deficit court-fee and in this way the learned District Judge allowed time, one after another, on the prayers of the defendant till the deficit court fee was filed on 8-9-1993. The proviso under rule 11 of Order VII of the Code of Civil Procedure prescribed the period of time thich the court authorised to give for the purpose of correction of the plaint or memo of appeal or for supplying the requisite stamp papers ie court-fees. This proviso which was added after rule 11 of Order VII of the Code of ci vii Procedure reads as under: "Provided that the time fixed by the court for the correction of the valuation or supplying of the requisite stamp paper shall not exceed twenty-one days."
